paper.title: Joint Value Estimation and Bidding in Repeated First-Price Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: JVEB in repeated first-price auctions, full-information HOB feedback
unmapped: First-price auction bidding: bid b_t in [0,1]; payoff 1[b_t>=M_t](v_{t,1}-b_t)+1[b_t<M_t]v_{t,0}
Value is a treatment effect: only the potential outcome of the realized treatment (win/lose) is observed
Linear treatment effect E[v_{t,1}-v_{t,0}|x_t]=theta^T x_t with ||theta||<=1, ||x_t||<=1
Highest other bid M_t is revealed every round (full-information HOB feedback)
Unconfoundedness: treatment effect independent of M_t given x_t; conditional independence over time given contexts
HOB CDF G_t is time-varying (depends on context) and L-Lipschitz (density bounded by L); learner knows L
Learner has access to a HOB CDF estimation oracle with known Bernstein-type confidence sequence delta_t (Abstraction 1)
Regret against dynamic oracle bidding the per-round optimal bid knowing theta and G_t, sup over {G_t, x_t}
settings.definition_quote: The bidder then submits a bid $b_t\in \R_+$, while the highest other bid (HOB) in that round is denoted by $M_t\in \R_+$. If $b_t\ge M_t$, the bidder wins the auction, and receives an outcome value $v_{t,1}$... If $b_t < M_t$, the bidder loses the auction, and receives an outcome value $v_{t,0}$... Full-information: the HOB $M_t$ is always revealed to the bidder at the end of time $t$.

symbols.Delta_HOB: HOB estimation error parameter 1 + sum_t delta_t^2 from Abstraction 1

conditions: Assumptions 2.1-2.4 (linear treatment effect, unconfoundedness, conditional independence, L-bounded HOB density)
HOB estimation oracle satisfying Abstraction 1 with known delta_t

source.label: thm:main-lte
source.quote: Suppose the bidder implements Abstraction \ref{ass:est_oracle_bern}. Under Assumptions \ref{assump:linear}--\ref{ass:Gt}, there is an algorithm $\pi_{\mathrm{lte}}$ (with the knowledge of the confidence bound $\delta_t$ at time $t$ and the knowledge of $L$) that achieves the expected regret $\Reglte(\pi_{\mathrm{lte}}) = \widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\Delta dT})$, where $\Delta := 1 + \sum_{t=1}^T \delta_t^2$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected payoffs \bar r_t against dynamic oracle, hence pseudo-regret. Plug-and-play bound.

source.label: thm:linear_te_reg_upper
source.quote: Let $\pi$ be the bidding strategy \cref{alg:master_alg_te}. Then under Assumptions \ref{assump:linear}--\ref{ass:Gt}, the policy $\pi$ achieves an expected regret $\Reglte(\pi) = O\parr*{\sqrt{\Delta dT}\log^3 T}$.

conditions: i.i.d. HOBs (empirical CDF oracle with delta_t = O~(1/sqrt t))

source.quote: When $M_t$ is i.i.d., Bernstein's concentration shows that \cref{ass:est_oracle_bern} holds for the empirical CDF with $\delta_t=\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{t})$. Then $\Delta=\widetilde{O}(1)$, and \cref{thm:main-lte} achieves a regret upper bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{dT})$ for i.i.d. HOBs.

results.notes: Consequence of Theorem 2.5 stated in text, not a separate formal statement. Same bound holds for known HOBs (Delta=1).

conditions: Linear HOB model M_t = phi^T x_t + eta_t with ||phi||<=1
eta_t i.i.d. zero-mean sigma^2-sub-Gaussian with flat tail and bounded second derivative of CDF (Assumption 2.6)

source.label: lem:linear_hob_error
source.quote: Let Assumptions \ref{ass:noconfounding}--\ref{ass:flat_noise_tail} hold. Under full-information HOB feedback, there exists a CDF estimator $\widehat{G}_t$ that satisfies \cref{ass:est_oracle_bern} with the HOB error parameter $\Delta=\widetildeO(d)$. ... Therefore, \cref{thm:main-lte} achieves a regret upper bound of $\widetilde{O}(d\sqrt{T})$

results.notes: Combination of Lemma 2.7 and Theorem 2.5 stated in text.

conditions: hard instance: v_{t,0}=0, v_{t,1} Bernoulli, i.i.d. known HOB mixture of uniforms

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{assump:linear}--\ref{ass:Gt}, even if $G_t$ is perfectly known, the following lower bounds hold: when $T\ge d^2$, $\inf_\pi \Reglte(\pi) = \Omega(\sqrt{dT})$.

results.notes: Holds for any HOB feedback since G_t known.

symbols.T_0: burn-in time after which the HOB oracle satisfies Abstraction 2
symbols.xi: bias parameter of the HOB estimation oracle (Abstraction 2)

conditions: HOB oracle satisfies Abstraction 2 for t >= T_0 with ||delta_t||_inf <= c for a small constant depending only on L

source.label: thm:main-lte-binary
source.quote: Suppose there is some $T_0$ such that for every $t\ge T_0$, the bidder implements Abstraction \ref{ass:est_oracle_weaker_bern} with $\|\delta_t\|_\infty \le c$ for a small constant $c$ depending only on $L$. Under Assumptions \ref{assump:linear}--\ref{ass:Gt}, there is an algorithm $\pi_{\mathrm{bin}}$ that achieves the expected regret $\widetilde{O}(T_0 + \sqrt{\Delta dT} + \xi T)$

source.label: thm:main-lte-binary-iid
source.quote: Consider the binary HOB feedback and i.i.d. HOBs. Under Assumptions \ref{assump:linear}--\ref{ass:Gt}, there is an oracle implementation of \cref{ass:est_oracle_weaker_bern} with $T_0 = \widetilde{O}(T^{2/3}), \Delta = \widetilde{O}(d^{-1/3}T^{1/3}), \xi = \widetilde{O}(d^{1/3}T^{-1/3})$. Consequently, there is an algorithm $\pi_{\mathrm{bin}}$ achieving the expected regret $\widetilde{O}(d^{1/3}T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Paper claims a matching Omega(d^{1/3}T^{2/3}) lower bound informally by embedding Balseiro et al. instance; not a formal statement, not recorded.

source.label: thm:exp3_fpa_regret_upper_bound
source.quote: When $\log|\Bcal|< (e-1)T$, EXP3-FPA-TE with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\log|\Bcal|}{(4e-2)T}}\in\parr*{0,\frac{1}{2}}$ achieves expected regret $\E[\max_{b_*\in\Bcal}\sum_{t=1}^T r_t(b_*) - \sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{b\in\Bcal}p_t(b) r_t(b)] \leq \sqrt{(4e-2)\log|\Bcal|T}$.

results.notes: K = |B| size of the finite bid set. Expectation outside max, so expected_regret.

source.quote: Let $\Bcal = \bra*{\frac{k}{T}:k\in[T]}\subseteq[0,1]$. Let $\pi$ be the resulting bidding strategy of \cref{alg:EXP3_FPA} running on this discretization with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\log(T)}{(4e-2)T}}$. Then under Assumptions \ref{ass:noconfounding}--\ref{ass:Gt}, the policy $\pi$ achieves expected regret $\Reglte_{\text{static}}(\pi) =O\parr*{\sqrt{T\log T}}$.

results.notes: Static regret defined via expected rewards against best fixed bid; proof gives 2L+1+sqrt((4e-2)T log T).

conditions: M_t i.i.d. with known distribution 1/2 Unif([0,1/100]) + 1/2 Unif([1/8-1/200,1/8+1/200])

source.label: thm:lower_bound_adv
source.quote: Consider a special instance with i.i.d. $v_{t,1}\sim \mathrm{Bern}(\mu)$ for an unknown $\mu\in [0,1]$, $v_{t,0}\equiv 0$, and i.i.d. $M_t$ following a known distribution ... Then for some absolute constant $c>0$, it holds that $\inf_{\pi}\sup_{\mu\in [0,1]} \sum_{t=1}^T ( \max_{b_*\in [0,1]} \E[r_t(b_*)] - \E[r_t(b_t)] ) \ge c\sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Without contexts the best fixed bid equals the per-round optimal bid.
